criteria.evidence: PendingTailoringIds.idFor(runId, applicationId) returns the run key tailoring.request.<runId> if present. Otherwise it adopts or mints the per-application pointer tailoring.request.unfinished.<applicationId> and writes the run key. Both keys are in the DataStore-backed MockStateStore, so they survive process death. sameRunIdResendsTheSameRequestIdAfterProcessDeath and aSucceededJobKeepsItsRequestIdForTheSameRun prove that one runId keeps one requestId. Both key kinds share the tailoring.request. prefix. SignOutCleaner.clear() calls removeWithPrefix("tailoring.request."). Sign-out calls cleaner.clear(). An account switch in RemoteSignInGateway.signIn calls cleaner.clear() and then wipeAll() (store.clear()). A UUID runId cannot collide with the literal unfinished.<applicationId> key. Two applications never share a pointer: aDifferentApplicationNeverAdoptsAnotherApplicationsPointer.

Read as D66 sets it out: a new runId after a finished run gets a new requestId (aNewRunIdAfterASucceededRunSendsANewRequestId, aNewRunIdAfterAFailedRunSendsANewRequestId, aNewRunIdSendsANewRequestId). A new runId after an abandoned unfinished run resends the abandoned requestId (aNewRunIdResendsTheRequestIdOfAnAbandonedUnfinishedRun). That test filters the POSTs out of POST/GET-poll/POST and asserts one distinct id. It fails at 9ea0c473.

RemoteResumeTailor.kt:52-60. SUCCEEDED settles only the pointer and keeps the run key. FAILED, or SUCCEEDED without a result, clears the pointer and the run key. The catch clears both only for non-RESUMABLE AiExceptions. Cancellation and non-AiException errors keep both. Interleavings of two taps r1 and r2 on one application (be-all start() returns an existing (user, requestId) row before reserveCredit; only RUNNING->SUCCEEDED spends): (a) r1 RUNNING, user goes Back (VM cancelled, pointer kept), r2 adopts J1: 1 job, 1 credit, J1 result. (b) r1 abandoned after a poll drop or Timeout: same as (a). (c) process death, r1 restored: run key -> J1, 1 job, 1 credit. (d) process death with the task removed, r2: adopts J1, 1 job, 1 credit, also when J1 finished SUCCEEDED while the app was dead. (e) r1 SUCCEEDED, then r2: pointer settled, new J2, 2 credits for 2 shown results (intended re-tailor). (f) r1 FAILED, then r2: pointer cleared, new J2, 1 credit. (g) J1 failed INTERRUPTED server-side while the app was dead, then r2: adopts J1, the server returns the FAILED row, the user sees one failure and 0 credits are charged. clear(r2) removes the pointer and r2's key, so Retry (replace with the same r2, D56) mints a fresh id: 1 credit on success. This is acceptable: no charge, one extra tap, and the failure shown is real. (h) A non-resumable failure from start() (NoCredit, AllowanceExhausted, InvalidInput, QuotaExceeded, SignInRequired) happens before a row exists, so clearing is correct. A non-resumable failure during polling (SignInRequired or AccountDeleted from GET) clears the pointer while J1 may still run. This is unchanged from base, which cleared the per-application key in the same catch, so this diff does not cause it. No stuck state: the pointer is written only at mint. Every finish observed by the client clears it, and a stale RUNNING row is failed INTERRUPTED by reconcileInterrupted. A pointer id the server never saw (429 or offline at start) creates exactly one row when resent. Round-1 balance-1 case: r2 now resends J1's id, gets the existing row before reserveCredit, and never gets a 402.

This round did not change the runner. Skip rule question: with adoption, J1's result is stored under runId r2. Suppose r1 later ran again. r1's run key still points to J1, because a run key is cleared only on FAILED or non-resumable. The server would return the stored J1 row: no reserve, no spend, no charge. Prod record() only refreshes the ledger. The re-run is also unreachable from the UI. Tailoring(r1) is replaced by TailorFailedNavKey or the result. The failure screen offers only Try again (replace with the same runId) and Go back, so no Tailoring(r1) entry can sit under r2. navigateToTailoring ignores a re-tap while the same application's Tailoring is on top. Adopted stale content stays truthful: TailorResumeUseCase re-verifies every proposed bullet, summary and skill against the current confirmed profile and quick answer. A bullet whose source fact was deleted after r1 is dropped.

This round made no demo-path changes. Process death traced again with the pointer. Between the pointer write and the run-key write: the restore reads the pointer and gets the same id. Between the server SUCCEEDED and the upsert: the run key is kept, so restoring r1 returns J1 with no charge. A relaunch with the task removed and a new tap also hits a pointer that is not yet settled. Only a death in the milliseconds between settle() and the upsert loses J1's result. Base had the same window, because it cleared on finish.

Unchanged since round 1 (theApplicationsQuickAnswerReachesTheTailor). With adoption, a quick answer changed between r1 and r2 is accepted by D66. TailorResumeUseCase still checks answer-backed bullets against the current answer.

findings.rule: Review checklist 5 / D64: an edited test must not weaken its assertion; c1 requires sign-out to wipe the pending tailoring request ids
findings.trigger: The test now mints with idFor("run-1", "app-1") and checks with idFor("run-2", "app-1"). The run-2 key never existed, so the check passes as soon as the unfinished pointer is gone. Change SignOutCleaner.clear() to removeWithPrefix("tailoring.request.unfinished.") and the test stays green while every tailoring.request.<runId> key survives sign-out. At 9ea0c473 the same assertion re-read the minted key, so it proved the run key was wiped. Impact is small, because account switch also runs wipeAll() and a surviving run key is reused only by the same user, but the assertion no longer covers the key kind it covered before.
findings.title: SignOutCleanerTest's edited assertion no longer proves that sign-out wipes the per-run request key
findings.proof: Use run-1 for the second call: assertThat(tailoringIds.idFor("run-1", "app-1")).isNotEqualTo(firstId). This fails if either key kind survives the wipe: a surviving run key returns firstId directly, and a surviving pointer returns firstId through adoption.
